heard: Critics swore the radiation belts would fry the Apollo crews. In 1958, Explorer 1 helped discover these two massive zones trapped by Earth's magnetic field. Named after physicist James Van Allen, the inner region holds energetic protons while the outer contains high-energy electrons. Skeptics argued that passing through these radioactive zones would prove fatal for human travelers. NASA trajectory planners designed high-speed routes through the thinnest parts of the belts. Protected by aluminum hulls and moving at roughly 25,000 miles per hour, astronauts spent only 30 minutes in the dense regions.
